C. de Propaganda Fide, 1901) printing are public domain in the United States by expiration of that identified historical publication's term, under the assessment in src/sources/inventories/papal-documents-rights-v1.toml. The uncorrected mechanical OCR adds no original literary authorship; it is not an image collation or a newly authored text. Exact hashes identify the unchanged delivery. Incidental provider and library marks remain distinct from the historical wording and outside Triptych's CC BY 4.0 grant. Any identified Google usage-guidelines prose or digitizer stamp is governed by the separate settled src/sources/inventories/google-usage-guidelines-rights-v1.toml assessment, without a general Google or provider licence. This historical-text assessment does not clear other unreviewed components of the complete PDF wrapper; that whole-PDF artifact remains remote with unresolved wrapper rights. No worldwide public-domain claim is made.

documents.source_note: Rome: Ex Typographia Polyglotta S. C. de Propaganda Fide, 1901. Uncorrected, uncollated OCR transcription of the identified constituent. Complete papal body; editorial caption or non-substantive publishing furniture omitted as separately identified in the source review. Fragment: the printed witness abbreviates the remaining clauses with “(Sequuntur clausulae etc.)”. Uncorrected OCR of the papal text; edition numeral, genre label, synopsis, running title and provenance citation omitted. Missing content: The printing breaks off the dispositive clause on the consecration of the coadjutor after “professionem catholicae fidei iuxta articulos a sede Nostra propositos etc.” and states “(Sequuntur clausulae etc.)” (LF32096–32098); the remaining faculty clauses and the non obstantibus clauses are not printed in this witness. The dating clause follows.
